terminal_tool.description: Terminal Tool enables interactive control of terminal sessions for programs like Python REPL, Node REPL, or Claude Code CLI.

sections.title: Terminal Tool Overview
sections.content:
The terminal tool allows you to:
- Open and manage interactive terminal sessions
- Send input to running programs
- Read output from terminal sessions
- Control program execution (stop, close)
- List active sessions

Useful for: Python REPL, Node.js REPL, CLI tools, interactive programs

sections.title: Terminal Actions
sections.content:
Available actions:

1. open: Start new terminal session
   - Required: command (e.g., "python3", "node", "claude")
   - Optional: args (array), cwd (working directory)
   - Returns: session_id for subsequent operations

2. send: Send input AND read response
   - Required: session_id, input (text to send)
   - Automatically appends newline and waits for output (2s timeout)
   - Returns: NEW output from the command
   - This is your PRIMARY action - it both sends and reads

3. read: Read output without sending
   - Required: session_id
   - Use when: checking output without sending new commands
   - Waits for new output (1s timeout)
   - Returns: NEW output since last read

4. stop: Send Ctrl+C signal
   - Required: session_id
   - Interrupts running command

5. close: Terminate session
   - Required: session_id
   - Closes terminal and cleans up

6. list: View active sessions
   - Returns: array of session info (id, command, timestamps)

sections.title: Usage Examples
Best Practices
sections.content:
- Keep sessions organized: Use descriptive session tracking
- Wait for output: Allow time for programs to process (500ms typical)
- Clean up: Always close sessions when done
- Handle errors: Check session existence before operations
- Session IDs: Store and reuse for the same terminal

Limitations:
- Sessions persist until explicitly closed
- Output buffering may have delays
- No TTY emulation (some programs may behave differently)
